findings.class: quote/gloss span parity (E-17 gloss overshoot; pre-existing, not repair-installed, not docketed)
findings.defective_text: (oshb:Ps.62.6) אַ֣ךְ לֵ֭אלֹהִים דּ֣וֹמִּי נַפְשִׁ֑י “My soul, wait in silence for God alone, for my expectation is from him.” (web:Ps.62.5)
findings.byte_evidence: The Hebrew run is tokens 1-4 of oshb:Ps.62.6 (collate.py --ref oshb:Ps.62.6 returns tier byte), but the paired English is the WHOLE of web:Ps.62.5, whose closing clause 'for my expectation is from him' renders oshb:Ps.62.6 tokens 5-7 כִּי מִ֝מֶּ֗נּוּ תִּקְוָתִֽי (byte tier, spliced from verse_map_oshb.json) which the quoted run does not reach; the same overshoot sits one clause earlier, where the run (oshb:Ps.62.2) אַ֣ךְ אֶל אֱ֭לֹהִים דּֽוּמִיָּ֣ה is tokens 1-4 of oshb:Ps.62.2 (tier byte) while the paired “My soul rests in God alone” (web:Ps.62.1) also renders token 5, נַפְשִׁ֑י (byte tier). Both English quotes are themselves verbatim WEB (check_web_quotes.py: 3 quotes, 0 flags, GREEN) and both oshb/web refs are crosswalk-correct, so the defect is span parity only.
findings.proposed_cure: Re-cut each pair so the English stops where the Hebrew run stops (or extend the run), e.g. pair the four-token run at oshb:Ps.62.6 with only “My soul, wait in silence for God alone”.

findings.class: tier-vocabulary precision (accent characterization vs the toolkit's accent_stripped tier)
findings.defective_text: oshb:Ps.62.7’s own tokens 6-7 are skeleton-identical to oshb:Ps.62.3’s, differing only in accents
findings.byte_evidence: Skeleton identity is byte-true: token 6 is לֹא at oshb:Ps.62.3 against לֹ֣א at oshb:Ps.62.7 (adds U+05A3 munach) and token 7 is אֶמּ֥וֹט against אֶמּֽוֹט, both pairs collapsing to the same consonants at skeleton tier (consonantal_index / ps_lib.skeleton), and no vowel or consonant differs. But the token-7 difference is U+05A5 merkha against U+05BD, and ps_lib.ACCENTS strips U+0591-U+05AF ONLY, RETAINING U+05BD, so the pair is NOT accent_stripped-identical in this toolkit's tier vocabulary even though U+05BD is verse-final silluq here; the row's named tier (skeleton) is the correct, non-over-tiered one, so the wording is loose rather than the tier claim being false.
findings.proposed_cure: Say 'differing only in cantillation marks' and keep the skeleton tier, or drop the accent characterization altogether, since the toolkit's accent_stripped tier retains U+05BD and the pair does not collate there.
